## Process monitoring config

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
PROCESS_MONITORING_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 5
```

</details>

How often, in seconds, the process monitor checks for processes starting
or stopping. A lower value detects changes sooner but uses slightly more
CPU.

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
EXCLUDED_PROCESSES = {'sudo','python'}
```

</details>

Process names that should be ignored by process monitoring. This
prevents the app from recording its own helper processes or other
unimportant background processes.

## Fore-ground application monitoring config

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
FG_APP_MONITORING_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 2
```

</details>

How often, in seconds, the foreground tracker samples the active
window/application. Lower values give more accurate switch timing but
create more polling work.

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
FG_APP_MONITORING_MIN_IDLE_SECONDS = 60
```

</details>

Number of seconds without user input before normal foreground time is
counted as idle rather than time spent in the active application.

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
STREAMING_APP_MIN_IDLE_SECONDS = {'youtube': 600, 'netflix': 600, 'twitch': 600}
```

</details>

Per-streaming-app idle thresholds. These allow an app such as YouTube,
Netflix, or Twitch to remain counted as active longer before being
treated as idle—for example while the user watches a video without
interacting.

<summary>Exported source</summary>

Whether reports may display recorded window titles. Turning this off is

foreground-time statistics.
